note: Nested click fixed in #95; WebKit touch coverage and the remaining touch fix added here.
Dropup positioning and scroll regression tests already exist.
Both adapters now skip preventDefault for explicitly noncancelable wheel events and retain it for cancelable events.
The fork exposes one named combobox at a time, hides inactive dropdown semantics, keeps option state current, and restores the closed control focus on Escape.
The fork exposes current combobox, listbox, option, expansion, and selection state and announces localized result counts during search.
Search listens for completed input values, waits for IME composition to end, and does not treat composition confirmation as option selection.
Covered by the composition-aware input search fix tracked with issue 2663.
Covered by the input-event search fallback tracked with issue 2663.
Home, End, Page Up, and Page Down navigate available results in both adapters while preserving caret movement in nonempty search input.
The report shows an inline-script CSP error; need an isolated demo to attribute it to Chosen.
Reproduced jQuery's active-field retap failure in iPad WebKit and added a touch regression.
Active queries now survive chosen:updated in both adapters; browser regressions added.
Clearing a single select with chosen:updated and pressing Tab kept its value empty in Chrome.
Dynamic options respected max_selected_options: 3 and fired chosen:maxselected for a fourth choice.
Active multiple selects reopen on repeated mouse clicks in both adapters, complementing the existing real iPad WebKit retap coverage.
Mobile failure report has no reproduction steps or browser details.
The empty multi-select results drop is hidden without changing open-state events or search behavior.
Single deselection clears the option's selected property and submitted value; the original selected HTML attribute remains as markup.
After deselection, the option is unselected and querySelectorAll finds no search-choice node.
Opening a second spaced select closes the first dropdown in Chrome.
A source select with zero measurable width gives its Chosen container auto width instead of an inline 0px width; both adapters have regressions.
A removed option made a stale result crash selection; both adapters now refresh stale results.
Both adapters recover after an empty search is cleared and select an existing option without stale-index errors; direct regressions cover the reported sequence.
A select inside an open Shadow DOM kept its dropdown open after clicking in Chrome.
Replacing options in the same select and triggering chosen:updated works repeatedly; replacing the select node requires initializing Chosen on the new node.
Focused single and multiple controls use the browser's native outline, with Sass variables for customization.
Current label handling uses an element reference and never calls form_field_label as a function.
Multiple search inputs now expose placeholder text only through the standard placeholder attribute.
The fork README lists the distributed jQuery, Prototype, and CSS files and includes npm and Composer installation commands.
Appending options and firing chosen:updated is covered in both adapters, including preserving an active search.
The maintained fork publishes current releases as chosen-jjj; it cannot backfill releases under Harvest's npm package.
The report does not include option markup, an expected value, or a reproduction that distinguishes an HTML entity from option text.
Both adapters now rebuild from restored native select values when browser history fires pageshow.
Opening results focuses the search input across the maintained jQuery matrix, including jQuery 4.
The fork initializes Chosen on mobile user agents and covers touch opening, selection, removal, and retapping.
Both adapters already fire chosen:no_results with the Chosen instance when a search has no matches.
Accent-insensitive matching and highlighting are covered in both adapters, with normalize_search_text available for custom normalization.
Both adapters now expose browser_is_supported before initialization.
The backspace_deletes_choices option disables keyboard removal without changing the existing single_backstroke_delete behavior.
Selected disabled options render without removal controls and backspace skips them in both adapters.
The fork copies accessible names and descriptions, preserves titles, and supports copying option data attributes through parser_config.
The report is specific to IE 11 and JAWS 18; neither environment is in the maintained browser matrix.
Blank options with nonempty values remain selectable; only options with empty text and values are placeholders.
Open dropdowns close when the browser window loses focus, preventing another Chosen from opening alongside a stale dropdown.
Required selects remain programmatically focusable so native constraint validation can focus the invalid control and display its message.
The options guide documents the CSS override for bold search matches, and Sass variables expose the highlight style without changing defaults.
The readonly attribute makes Chosen non-editable without disabling the source select, so its selected value remains enabled for form submission.
Stay-open multiple selects preserve their results scroll position and highlight the next nearby option without changing active-search behavior.
A select placeholder attribute now supplies the default text when data-placeholder is absent, with both adapters covered.
Modern browsers use native standard wheel scrolling; manual mousewheel and DOMMouseScroll handling remains only as a legacy fallback.
Single-select result selection now blurs the hidden search input and returns focus to the visible control, dismissing the mobile keyboard in both adapters.
Result selection no longer refocuses Chosen after a change handler moves focus to another field.
Initializing Chosen on a focused select transfers focus to the generated control without opening the dropdown, preserving native autofocus behavior.
Delayed multiple-select activation now verifies that its search input still owns focus, preventing rapid Tab navigation from reopening earlier controls.
Single selects with allow_single_deselect can now be cleared from the focused control with Backspace or Delete in both adapters.
The chosen:updated event now mirrors changes to the source select title onto the visible Chosen container, including title removal.
The chosen:updated event now recalculates single-deselect eligibility when a true empty first option is added or removed dynamically.
When inherit_select_classes is enabled, chosen:updated now replaces inherited source classes while preserving Chosen's own live state classes.
A selected option whose label matches the placeholder text now remains selected styling instead of receiving the chosen-default class.
An empty-search max_shown_results window now shifts to include the selected single option without exceeding the configured result limit.
